title: The Name Reverted After the Divorce
scenario_text: Lindholm Insurance's People Ops team is investigating a duplicate-payee alert raised by payroll. Workday shows one active employee record E-32001 "Petra Halvorsen-Ruud," and payroll flagged an apparent second beneficiary "Petra Halvorsen" appearing on a garnishment court order. HR's concern is whether a second employee exists or whether records were mistakenly split. Evidence: E-32001 has national ID ending 5140, DOB 1985-03-22, direct-deposit account ending 3092, and a name-change event logged 2024-03-15 with note "legal name change following divorce decree; surname reverts from Halvorsen-Ruud to Halvorsen." The court garnishment order names "Petra Halvorsen," cites the same national ID ending 5140 and the same DOB 1985-03-22, and post-dates the decree. Okta still shows the login phalvorsenruud@lindholm.com (not yet updated). The prior married surname "Halvorsen-Ruud" appears on benefits enrollment records from 2019-2024; the maiden/current surname "Halvorsen" appears on the pre-2019 record and the new post-decree documents. There is exactly one national ID, one DOB, and one direct-deposit account across every record. Payroll must decide whether to create a new employee record for "Petra Halvorsen" or update the existing one, and how to apply the garnishment. Benefits enrollment, tax withholding, and PTO accrual are all keyed to a single employee ID today, so any decision to spawn a second record would immediately ripple into those downstream systems and the pending court-ordered deduction.
question: How should payroll resolve the "Petra Halvorsen" garnishment against the existing record?
choices: Create a new employee record for Petra Halvorsen and apply the garnishment there, since the surname on the court order does not match the current Workday display name.

Recognize "Petra Halvorsen" and "Petra Halvorsen-Ruud" as the same employee (E-32001) after a post-divorce legal name change, update the record and Okta to the reverted surname, and apply the garnishment to E-32001.
Reject the garnishment as unmatched because the payee name differs from the name on file, and return it to the court.
Split payroll across two records so each surname variant receives part of the pay and the garnishment applies to only one.
